addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-cleaner: Use this agent after writing or changing C/C++ code, to bring it inside the complexity + coverage budget and prove it with real measurements. It builds with --coverage, runs the tests, scores every function you touched with CRAP = CC^2*(1-coverage)^3 + CC alongside cognitive complexity, then fixes what is over budget by adding the missing tests or splitting a genuinely tangled function - and reports the before/after numbers. Delegate to it whenever you have just written a non-trivial C/C++ function, whenever the user mentions complexity, cyclomatic or cognitive complexity, CRAP, code coverage, gcov, 'make this testable' or 'clean this up', and whenever a CRAP/coverage gate has to pass before work counts as done. Its whole build-and-measure loop is noisy, so running it here keeps that noise out of the main conversation.

Examples:

- assistant: *writes a new parser in src/config.cpp*
  assistant: "Now let me hand this to the code-cleaner agent to measure it and close any coverage gaps"

- user: "is dispatch_event getting too complicated?"
  assistant: "I'll use the code-cleaner agent to measure it rather than guess" (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---
name: gitea-issue-tracker
description: andesim tickets are Gitea issues at gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim; use the `tea` CLI (login "andes") with --repo nick/hybrid_sim and --description, not --body.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

"Ticket" for the andesim repo means a **Gitea issue** on the origin remote
`https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim`. There is no in-repo ticket
directory and no `.gitea/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`; the tracker was empty until
2026-09-06.

Use the **`tea` CLI** (`~/.local/bin/tea`, v0.15.1, installed 2026-09-06).
The login is already configured under the name `andes` (created from the
`~/.git-credentials` password; tea minted its own access token on the server).

```sh
tea issues create --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim \
  --title "..." --description "$BODY"
tea issues list --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim
```

Two gotchas, both cost a retry:

- The body flag is **`--description` / `-d`**, NOT `--body`.
- **`--repo nick/hybrid_sim` is required.** Auto-detection from the local git
  remote fails ("remote repository required") because the origin URL carries
  userinfo: `https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git`.

The repo has **no labels and no milestones defined**, so don't pass
`--labels`/`--milestone` until some are created. Bodies render GitHub-flavored
markdown (tables work).

Roadmap item IDs (`U10h`, `U11`, `FR-109`, ...) from the `ROADMAP_*.md` files
are the natural ticket titles — see [[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]].

===== ISSUE #24 =====
TITLE: release: one podman build must produce a working AndeSim image (BLOCKED: private-repo auth undecided)
STATE: open
> **NOT READY TO IMPLEMENT.** One product decision is unresolved — see the section below. Do not start this work, and do not choose an answer to the open question, until that section has been replaced with a decision.

## Problem

AndeSim v0.1.0 is delivered as a repository plus a container definition. Users build the image themselves; no prebuilt image is published, and there is no registry. For that delivery to be worth anything, building the image must be the *only* thing the user has to do.

Today the container definition builds only the AndeSim driver. QEMU, the cycle-accurate engine, and the RISC-V toolchain are all expected to already exist on the user's machine and be mounted in at run time. That means a user must first build QEMU themselves and build the engine themselves — which is exactly the setup burden the container was supposed to remove. Handing someone a container definition that still requires them to do all the hard parts first solves nothing.

## Required Behavior

A single image build, given only a path to a RISC-V toolchain, must produce an image that runs AndeSim with no further preparation.

- **The build obtains and builds the QEMU that AndeSim uses.** The user does not build QEMU beforehand.
- **The build obtains and builds the cycle-accurate engine.** Exactly one engine is built: `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`. No other engine is built, because building an engine is the slowest step of the image build and no other engine is supported in this release.
- **The toolchain is supplied by the user as a build parameter naming a path, and ends up inside the image.** After the build, no toolchain path has to be supplied again — not at run time, not ever. The user names it once, when they build.
- **The resulting image contains everything needed for every supported mode.** Nothing has to be mounted in for a normal bare-metal run.

A prerequisite that must be **stated to the user, not worked around**: building the image requires access to the Andes RD-SW repositories, because the engine's RTL comes from them. A user without that access cannot build the image, and must be told so plainly rather than discovering it as a confusing failure partway through a long build.

## UNRESOLVED — blocks implementation

**How the image build authenticates to the private repositories has not been decided.**

The repositories the build must obtain are private, so the build needs credentials. Three approaches were considered and none has been adopted:

- a build-time secret that is consumed during the build and does not persist into the finished image;
- a credential passed as an ordinary build argument — considered and objected to, because it would remain visible in the finished image's build history to anyone who receives the image;
- requiring the user to clone the repositories on the host beforehand and supply them to the build — considered and objected to, because it re-imposes the setup burden this whole ticket exists to remove.

This is being tested before a decision is made. **Do not choose one.** When the decision is made it must be written into this ticket, and only then may implementation begin.

## Acceptance Scenarios

These scenarios describe the required behaviour once the open question above is resolved. They are not implementable until then.

```gherkin
Feature: One image build produces a working AndeSim

Scenario: A user with a toolchain and nothing else builds a working image
  Given a clean checkout of the AndeSim repository
  And a path to a RISC-V toolchain on the build machine
  And no QEMU built for AndeSim and no cycle-accurate engine built on that machine
  When I build the container image, naming only the toolchain path
  Then the build completes
  And the resulting image contains AndeSim, a working QEMU, and the "ax46mpv_fpga_l3" engine
  And the image contains a RISC-V toolchain

Scenario: A bare-metal run needs nothing mounted in
  Given an image built as above
  When I run a bare-metal workload using that image
  Then the run completes and reports a result
  And I mounted nothing into the container beyond my own working directory

Scenario: Only the supported engine is built
  Given an image built as above
  When I list the cycle-accurate engines available in the image
  Then "ax46mpv_fpga_l3" is present
  And no other cycle-accurate engine is present

Scenario: A user without repository access is told why
  Given a build machine whose user has no access to the Andes RD-SW repositories
  When I attempt to build the image
  Then the failure states that access to those repositories is required
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- Exactly one cycle-accurate engine is built: `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`.
- The toolchain path is a build-time parameter, not a run-time one.
- No image is published anywhere. There is no registry, and no prebuilt image is distributed; every user builds their own.
- Building requires access to the Andes RD-SW repositories. This is an accepted prerequisite of the product, to be documented, not engineered around.

## QA Procedure

1. On a machine with a RISC-V toolchain and no AndeSim-built QEMU and no built engine, take a clean checkout.
2. Build the image, supplying only the toolchain path.
3. Confirm the build completes, and that the image contains AndeSim, a QEMU able to run, the `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` engine, and a RISC-V toolchain.
4. Confirm no cycle-accurate engine other than `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is in the image.
5. Run a bare-metal workload using the image, mounting nothing but your own working directory. Confirm it reports a result.
6. Confirm no toolchain path had to be supplied at run time.
7. On a machine whose user lacks access to the Andes RD-SW repositories, attempt the build and confirm the failure says that access is required.

## Out of Scope

- Publishing the image to a registry.
- Building any engine other than `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`.
- Including llama.cpp or a model file in the image. Both are supplied by the user.
- Making the image usable by someone without access to the Andes RD-SW repositories.
- What the image excludes — that the image must carry no repository git history and no local configuration file with machine-specific paths is specified separately.

## Notes

Building the engine is the slowest step in the image build, which is why exactly one engine is built rather than all of them.

===== ISSUE #20 =====
TITLE: release: on Linux, andesim must run inside the container transparently, with shared memory sized to the run
STATE: open
## Problem

AndeSim v0.1.0 is delivered as a container image that each user builds themselves. That image holds everything a run needs: the driver, QEMU, the cycle-accurate engine, and a RISC-V toolchain. The user should never have to know a container is involved — they type an AndeSim command and get a cycle number.

Today only macOS gets that. On macOS the AndeSim entry point re-executes the command inside a container. On Linux it runs a locally built binary directly, so a Linux user of the image would have to compose container invocations by hand.

There is also a failure waiting for the first Linux user who runs hybrid mode inside a container. A hybrid run needs a shared memory region under `/dev/shm` that both the functional leg and the cycle-accurate leg map. A container gets 64 MB of `/dev/shm` by default. The standard tests already need 128 MB, and Linux-runtime workloads need several gigabytes. Without handling, the first hybrid run a user tries fails.

## Required Behavior

On Linux, when an AndeSim image is available, running the AndeSim entry point on the host must execute the requested command inside that image, and the user must not have to supply any container option:

- **Same command.** `andesim run --mode hybrid <elf>`, and every other supported command and option, must behave the same as if there were no container. The user types no container command and passes no container flag.
- **The working directory is visible.** The user's current working directory must be reachable from inside the container, so that an ELF named by a path under the working directory resolves, and any file the run writes appears in the user's directory afterwards with the path they expect.
- **Shared memory is sized automatically.** The container's `/dev/shm` must be sized from the guest memory size the run asks for. A run must never fail because the shared memory region was smaller than the run needed. The user must not have to pass a container option to make a hybrid run work, at any supported memory size.
- **A missing image is reported clearly.** If no AndeSim image is available, the entry point must say so in terms the user can act on — that an image must be built — rather than surfacing a raw container error.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: The container is invisible to a Linux user

Scenario: A hybrid run works with no container knowledge
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built and no AndeSim binary installed on the host
  And a program in my current working directory
  When I run the AndeSim run command in hybrid mode on that program
  Then the run completes
  And a cycle count is reported
  And I passed no container command and no container option

Scenario: Output lands in my own directory
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built
  When I run a command that writes an output file into my current working directory
  Then after the run the file exists in my working directory at the path I asked for

Scenario Outline: Shared memory is large enough for the requested guest memory
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built
  When I run a hybrid workload asking for <mem> of guest memory
  Then the run completes
  And it does not fail for want of shared memory

Examples:
  | mem   |
  | 128M  |
  | 1G    |
  | 8G    |

Scenario: No image has been built yet
  Given a Linux host with no AndeSim image
  When I run an AndeSim command
  Then the command fails with a message saying an image must be built first
  And the message is not a raw container runtime error
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- The default shared-memory allocation a container receives is 64 MB. The standard test suite needs at least 128 MB and Linux-runtime workloads need several gigabytes, so a fixed value cannot serve both; the size must follow the run's requested guest memory.
- macOS already runs commands inside a container. Its behaviour must not regress.

## QA Procedure

1. On a Linux host, build the AndeSim image. Make sure no AndeSim binary is installed on the host itself, so any success proves the container path was used.
2. From a directory containing a program, run a hybrid measurement with no container flags. Confirm a cycle count comes back.
3. Run a command that produces an output file. Confirm the file appears in the directory you ran from, at the path you asked for.
4. Run hybrid workloads at several guest memory sizes, including one well above 64 MB and one of several gigabytes. Confirm none fails for want of shared memory, and that you never had to pass a container option.
5. Rename or remove the image, then run any AndeSim command. Confirm the failure message tells you an image must be built, and is not a raw container error.
6. Repeat steps 2 and 3 on macOS to confirm no regression there.

## Out of Scope

- Publishing an image to a registry. v0.1.0 publishes no image; each user builds their own.
- What the image build itself does, which is specified separately.
- Running AndeSim natively on the host without a container. That path still exists for development and is unchanged by this ticket.

## Notes

Making the container invisible is the whole reason the image is worth building. If a user still has to compose container invocations, they are back to managing the same paths and options the image was meant to remove.

===== ISSUE #23 =====
TITLE: release: gate a release on a full green run - unit, contract, e2e, and a real image build
STATE: open
## Problem

AndeSim v0.1.0 begins a maintained release line: releases carry a version, are recorded in a changelog, and carry an expectation that they work. Releases happen when there is something worth releasing, not on a schedule.

There is currently nothing that decides whether a given commit is fit to be released. The project has no automated check of any kind — no continuous integration, no gate, no release procedure. Whether a release works is a matter of whoever cut it having remembered to run the tests.

A hand-maintained changelog and a version number, with nothing verifying that the thing being versioned actually works, is a maintained release line in name only.

## Required Behavior

A single command must decide whether the current tree is releasable, and if it is, produce the release.

**It must run, and require to pass, all four of:**

1. the unit tests
2. the contract tests
3. the end-to-end tests
4. an actual build of the container image — the image must really build, not merely be checked for syntax

**Its behaviour:**

- If any stage fails, the command exits non-zero and names which stage failed.
- It exits zero only when all four stages pass.
- **It must refuse to create a release tag when any stage failed.** A failed run must leave no tag and no changelog entry behind.
- When everything passes, it produces the release: a SemVer tag on the `llamacpp` branch, and a changelog entry for that version.
- It must be runnable at any time. Releases are ad-hoc; nothing schedules them.

The first release produced this way is `v0.1.0`.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: A release is gated on a full green run

Scenario: Everything passes
  Given a tree in which the unit, contract, and end-to-end tests all pass
  And the container image builds successfully from that tree
  When I run the release command for version "v0.1.0"
  Then it exits zero
  And a tag "v0.1.0" exists on the llamacpp branch
  And the changelog has an entry for "v0.1.0"

Scenario Outline: A failing stage blocks the release
  Given a tree in which the <stage> stage fails
  When I run the release command
  Then it exits non-zero
  And the output names "<stage>" as the stage that failed
  And no release tag was created
  And no changelog entry was added

Examples:
  | stage        |
  | unit         |
  | contract     |
  | end-to-end   |
  | image build  |

Scenario: The image build is real
  Given a tree whose container image definition is syntactically valid but fails partway through building
  When I run the release command
  Then it exits non-zero
  And the output names the image build as the stage that failed
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- Release tags are SemVer and are cut on the `llamacpp` branch.
- Releases are ad-hoc. The command must not depend on a scheduler, a timer, or a hosted automation service; it must be runnable on demand by a person.
- The first release is `v0.1.0`. Changelog entries begin there; earlier history is not reconstructed.

## QA Procedure

1. On a tree where everything is known good, run the release command for a test version. Confirm it exits zero, creates the tag on the `llamacpp` branch, and writes a changelog entry. Remove the test tag afterwards.
2. Deliberately break a unit test. Run the release command. Confirm it exits non-zero, names the unit stage, and creates no tag and no changelog entry. Restore the test.
3. Repeat step 2 for a contract test, for an end-to-end test, and for the container image build — breaking each in turn, confirming the correct stage is named, and confirming no tag or changelog entry is left behind.
4. Break the image build in a way that only shows up partway through building, rather than as an invalid definition. Confirm the command still catches it.
5. Confirm the command can be run twice in a row on a good tree without a scheduler or any external service.

## Out of Scope

- Continuous integration, hosted build automation, or anything that runs on a schedule. Releases are ad-hoc and this command is run by a person.
- Publishing an image to a registry, or publishing a release artefact anywhere. v0.1.0 publishes a tag and a repository; users build their own image.
- Reconstructing changelog entries for versions before `v0.1.0`.

## Notes

The image-build stage is what makes the gate meaningful for this product: AndeSim is delivered as a container definition that users build themselves, so a release whose image does not build is not a release at all — and that failure is invisible to any test suite that runs outside the image.

```gherkin
  And no QEMU built for AndeSim and no cycle-accurate engine built on that machine
  When I build the container image, naming only the toolchain path
  Then the build completes
  And the resulting image contains AndeSim, a working QEMU, and the "ax46mpv_fpga_l3" engine
  And the image contains a RISC-V toolchain

Scenario: A bare-metal run needs nothing mounted in
  Given an image built as above
  When I run a bare-metal workload using that image
  Then the run completes and reports a result
  And I mounted nothing into the container beyond my own working directory

Scenario: Only the supported engine is built
  Given an image built as above
  When I list the cycle-accurate engines available in the image
  Then "ax46mpv_fpga_l3" is present
  And no other cycle-accurate engine is present

Scenario: A user without repository access is told why
  Given a build machine whose user has no access to the Andes RD-SW repositories
  When I attempt to build the image
  Then the failure states that access to those repositories is required
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- Exactly one cycle-accurate engine is built: `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`.
- The toolchain path is a build-time parameter, not a run-time one.
- No image is published anywhere. There is no registry, and no prebuilt image is distributed; every user builds their own.
- Building requires access to the Andes RD-SW repositories. This is an accepted prerequisite of the product, to be documented, not engineered around.

## QA Procedure

1. On a machine with a RISC-V toolchain and no AndeSim-built QEMU and no built engine, take a clean checkout.
2. Build the image, supplying only the toolchain path.
3. Confirm the build completes, and that the image contains AndeSim, a QEMU able to run, the `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` engine, and a RISC-V toolchain.
4. Confirm no cycle-accurate engine other than `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is in the image.
5. Run a bare-metal workload using the image, mounting nothing but your own working directory. Confirm it reports a result.
6. Confirm no toolchain path had to be supplied at run time.
7. On a machine whose user lacks access to the Andes RD-SW repositories, attempt the build and confirm the failure says that access is required.

## Out of Scope

- Publishing the image to a registry.
- Building any engine other than `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`.
- Including llama.cpp or a model file in the image. Both are supplied by the user.
- Making the image usable by someone without access to the Andes RD-SW repositories.
- What the image excludes — that the image must carry no repository git history and no local configuration file with machine-specific paths is specified separately.

## Notes

Building the engine is the slowest step in the image build, which is why exactly one engine is built rather than all of them.

===== ISSUE #20 =====
TITLE: release: on Linux, andesim must run inside the container transparently, with shared memory sized to the run
STATE: open
## Problem

AndeSim v0.1.0 is delivered as a container image that each user builds themselves. That image holds everything a run needs: the driver, QEMU, the cycle-accurate engine, and a RISC-V toolchain. The user should never have to know a container is involved — they type an AndeSim command and get a cycle number.

Today only macOS gets that. On macOS the AndeSim entry point re-executes the command inside a container. On Linux it runs a locally built binary directly, so a Linux user of the image would have to compose container invocations by hand.

There is also a failure waiting for the first Linux user who runs hybrid mode inside a container. A hybrid run needs a shared memory region under `/dev/shm` that both the functional leg and the cycle-accurate leg map. A container gets 64 MB of `/dev/shm` by default. The standard tests already need 128 MB, and Linux-runtime workloads need several gigabytes. Without handling, the first hybrid run a user tries fails.

## Required Behavior

On Linux, when an AndeSim image is available, running the AndeSim entry point on the host must execute the requested command inside that image, and the user must not have to supply any container option:

- **Same command.** `andesim run --mode hybrid <elf>`, and every other supported command and option, must behave the same as if there were no container. The user types no container command and passes no container flag.
- **The working directory is visible.** The user's current working directory must be reachable from inside the container, so that an ELF named by a path under the working directory resolves, and any file the run writes appears in the user's directory afterwards with the path they expect.
- **Shared memory is sized automatically.** The container's `/dev/shm` must be sized from the guest memory size the run asks for. A run must never fail because the shared memory region was smaller than the run needed. The user must not have to pass a container option to make a hybrid run work, at any supported memory size.
- **A missing image is reported clearly.** If no AndeSim image is available, the entry point must say so in terms the user can act on — that an image must be built — rather than surfacing a raw container error.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: The container is invisible to a Linux user

Scenario: A hybrid run works with no container knowledge
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built and no AndeSim binary installed on the host
  And a program in my current working directory
  When I run the AndeSim run command in hybrid mode on that program
  Then the run completes
  And a cycle count is reported
  And I passed no container command and no container option

Scenario: Output lands in my own directory
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built
  When I run a command that writes an output file into my current working directory
  Then after the run the file exists in my working directory at the path I asked for

Scenario Outline: Shared memory is large enough for the requested guest memory
  Given a Linux host with an AndeSim image built
  When I run a hybrid workload asking for <mem> of guest memory
  Then the run completes
  And it does not fail for want of shared memory

Examples:
  | mem   |
  | 128M  |
  | 1G    |
  | 8G    |

Scenario: No image has been built yet
  Given a Linux host with no AndeSim image
  When I run an AndeSim command
  Then the command fails with a message saying an image must be built first
  And the message is not a raw container runtime error
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- The default shared-memory allocation a container receives is 64 MB. The standard test suite needs at least 128 MB and Linux-runtime workloads need several gigabytes, so a fixed value cannot serve both; the size must follow the run's requested guest memory.
- macOS already runs commands inside a container. Its behaviour must not regress.

## QA Procedure

1. On a Linux host, build the AndeSim image. Make sure no AndeSim binary is installed on the host itself, so any success proves the container path was used.
2. From a directory containing a program, run a hybrid measurement with no container flags. Confirm a cycle count comes back.
3. Run a command that produces an output file. Confirm the file appears in the directory you ran from, at the path you asked for.
4. Run hybrid workloads at several guest memory sizes, including one well above 64 MB and one of several gigabytes. Confirm none fails for want of shared memory, and that you never had to pass a container option.
5. Rename or remove the image, then run any AndeSim command. Confirm the failure message tells you an image must be built, and is not a raw container error.
6. Repeat steps 2 and 3 on macOS to confirm no regression there.

## Out of Scope

- Publishing an image to a registry. v0.1.0 publishes no image; each user builds their own.
- What the image build itself does, which is specified separately.
- Running AndeSim natively on the host without a container. That path still exists for development and is unchanged by this ticket.

## Notes

Making the container invisible is the whole reason the image is worth building. If a user still has to compose container invocations, they are back to managing the same paths and options the image was meant to remove.

===== ISSUE #23 =====
TITLE: release: gate a release on a full green run - unit, contract, e2e, and a real image build
STATE: open
## Problem

AndeSim v0.1.0 begins a maintained release line: releases carry a version, are recorded in a changelog, and carry an expectation that they work. Releases happen when there is something worth releasing, not on a schedule.

There is currently nothing that decides whether a given commit is fit to be released. The project has no automated check of any kind — no continuous integration, no gate, no release procedure. Whether a release works is a matter of whoever cut it having remembered to run the tests.

A hand-maintained changelog and a version number, with nothing verifying that the thing being versioned actually works, is a maintained release line in name only.

## Required Behavior

A single command must decide whether the current tree is releasable, and if it is, produce the release.

**It must run, and require to pass, all four of:**

1. the unit tests
2. the contract tests
3. the end-to-end tests
4. an actual build of the container image — the image must really build, not merely be checked for syntax

**Its behaviour:**

- If any stage fails, the command exits non-zero and names which stage failed.
- It exits zero only when all four stages pass.
- **It must refuse to create a release tag when any stage failed.** A failed run must leave no tag and no changelog entry behind.
- When everything passes, it produces the release: a SemVer tag on the `llamacpp` branch, and a changelog entry for that version.
- It must be runnable at any time. Releases are ad-hoc; nothing schedules them.

The first release produced this way is `v0.1.0`.

## Acceptance Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: A release is gated on a full green run

Scenario: Everything passes
  Given a tree in which the unit, contract, and end-to-end tests all pass
  And the container image builds successfully from that tree
  When I run the release command for version "v0.1.0"
  Then it exits zero
  And a tag "v0.1.0" exists on the llamacpp branch
  And the changelog has an entry for "v0.1.0"

Scenario Outline: A failing stage blocks the release
  Given a tree in which the <stage> stage fails
  When I run the release command
  Then it exits non-zero
  And the output names "<stage>" as the stage that failed
  And no release tag was created
  And no changelog entry was added

Examples:
  | stage        |
  | unit         |
  | contract     |
  | end-to-end   |
  | image build  |

Scenario: The image build is real
  Given a tree whose container image definition is syntactically valid but fails partway through building
  When I run the release command
  Then it exits non-zero
  And the output names the image build as the stage that failed
```

## Compatibility and Constraints

- Release tags are SemVer and are cut on the `llamacpp` branch.
- Releases are ad-hoc. The command must not depend on a scheduler, a timer, or a hosted automation service; it must be runnable on demand by a person.
- The first release is `v0.1.0`. Changelog entries begin there; earlier history is not reconstructed.

## QA Procedure

1. On a tree where everything is known good, run the release command for a test version. Confirm it exits zero, creates the tag on the `llamacpp` branch, and writes a changelog entry. Remove the test tag afterwards.
2. Deliberately break a unit test. Run the release command. Confirm it exits non-zero, names the unit stage, and creates no tag and no changelog entry. Restore the test.
3. Repeat step 2 for a contract test, for an end-to-end test, and for the container image build — breaking each in turn, confirming the correct stage is named, and confirming no tag or changelog entry is left behind.
4. Break the image build in a way that only shows up partway through building, rather than as an invalid definition. Confirm the command still catches it.
5. Confirm the command can be run twice in a row on a good tree without a scheduler or any external service.

## Out of Scope

- Continuous integration, hosted build automation, or anything that runs on a schedule. Releases are ad-hoc and this command is run by a person.
- Publishing an image to a registry, or publishing a release artefact anywhere. v0.1.0 publishes a tag and a repository; users build their own image.
- Reconstructing changelog entries for versions before `v0.1.0`.

## Notes

The image-build stage is what makes the gate meaningful for this product: AndeSim is delivered as a container definition that users build themselves, so a release whose image does not build is not a release at all — and that failure is invisible to any test suite that runs outside the image.

# andesim runtime image -- for run-only hosts (macOS via podman machine).
#
# Built ON LINUX (CI or a Linux workstation); macOS users only pull it:
#
#   podman build -f Dockerfile.runtime \
#     --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<verilator env image> \
#     -t andesim-runtime:latest .
#
# BASE_IMAGE is the vsim build environment from the external vsim repo's
# root Dockerfile (target `env`) -- the same image its build_vsim.sh builds
# (vsim-env:latest), so the Verilator/SystemC toolchain and QEMU build deps
# are already there.
# The publish registry/name is still an open question; consumers override
# the local default with ANDESIM_IMAGE.
#
# The whole repo is baked, fully built, at /opt/hybrid_sim, so the baked
# ./andesim resolves every artifact via its normal repo-relative paths
# (plugin, runtime). scripts/run_in_container.sh
# invokes that path as the entry; the user's cwd is bind-mounted only for
# ELF inputs and outputs.
ARG BASE_IMAGE=andes-vsim-env:latest
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

COPY . /opt/hybrid_sim
WORKDIR /opt/hybrid_sim

# Build: plugin -> driver -> runtime. Both QEMU and vsim are NOT built here --
# they are integrated as external prebuilt binaries; provide them at run time, e.g.
#   -v /path/to/qemu/build:/qemu:ro   -e VSIM_QEMU=/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
#   -v /path/to/vsim/build:/vsim:ro   -e VSIM_BIN_DIR=/vsim
# (the plugin builds against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h, so
# no QEMU source tree is needed; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning
# $VSIM_BIN_DIR). setup.sh is NOT used here -- it locates the external qemu/vsim,
# which are mounted at run time, not build time.
RUN make -C qemu_plugin \
 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
 && make -C runtime

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim"]
===== TREE =====

# Hybrid simulator per-host configuration.
#
# This file is the TEMPLATE (committed). On first `source ./setup.sh`,

# at the toolchain on your host; never commit your local edits.

# unconditionally, so the file's plain assignments overwrite any value

# before parsing the file -- on those paths exported values can win.

# AndeSim supports 64-bit RISC-V only. Every toolchain, QEMU binary and engine
# named below is a 64-bit one; there is nothing 32-bit to configure.

# Andes RISC-V GCC toolchain root (rv64). Must contain

# static-glibc test fixtures ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+ needs (and
# eventually llama-completion). Must contain bin/riscv64-linux-{gcc,g++,ld,...}.
# Leave unset if you are not working on the vlinux Linux-runtime effort.

# at $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (or override both via
# LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN / BONSAI_GGUF). Leave unset if you are not working

# longer builds QEMU; you build it yourself and point here. setup.sh validates
# the binary exists and exports VSIM_QEMU from this.

# Directory holding the externally-built vsim sim_* binaries. This project no
# longer nests vsim as a submodule; you build it in your own vsim checkout (its
# build_vsim.sh) and point here. setup.sh exports VSIM_BIN_DIR from this, and the

=== setup.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;

  fi

    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv64)"

    return 1

    err "no qemu-system-riscv64 under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64 (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1

    return 1

    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1

=== vsim Dockerfile ===
# verilator must be >= v5.026
FROM docker.io/verilator/verilator:v5.046 AS verilator


# Base environment with development tools
FROM ubuntu:24.04 AS env

WORKDIR /work

RUN \
  apt-get update && \
  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends \
  autoconf autoconf-archive automake autotools-dev bison ca-certificates clang \
  cmake curl flex g++ git help2man libboost-date-time-dev libboost-dev \
  libboost-filesystem-dev libboost-system-dev libfl-dev libfl2 libreadline-dev \
  libtool lld m4 make ninja-build patch perl perl-doc pkg-config vim \
  python3-dev python3-pybind11 ccache tclsh xz-utils zlib1g zlib1g-dev \
  python3-yaml && \
  apt-get clean && \
  rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/share/verilator /usr/local/share/verilator
COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin


# Common build preparation
FROM env AS build-prep

COPY ./CMakeLists.txt ./config.yaml /work/
COPY ./cmake/ /work/cmake/
COPY ./data/ /work/data/
COPY ./external/ /work/external/
COPY ./src/ /work/src/
COPY ./tools/ /work/tools/
COPY ./stubs/ /work/stubs/


# Builds vsim from source (release mode)
FROM build-prep AS build

ARG VERSION=""
RUN \
  cmake -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/work/vsim \
  -DVSIM_LINK_STATIC=ON \
  -DVSIM_VERSION_OVERRIDE=${VERSION} && \
  cmake --build build --target all && \
  cmake --install build

# Remove RTL, verilated objects and cpp, strip binaries
RUN \
  find build/V*/obj_sc -type f \( -name "*.v" -o -name "*.sv" -o -name "*.xml" -o -name "*.c" -o -name "*.cpp" -o -name "*.o" -o -name "*.d" \) -delete && \
  find build/V* -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 ! -name "obj_sc" -exec rm -rf {} + && \
  find /work/vsim/bin/ -type f -exec strip {} \;

# Reconfigure without verilator so the dev stage can relink without re-verilating
RUN \
  cmake -B build -G Ninja \
  -DVSIM_VERSION_OVERRIDE=${VERSION} \
  -DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON


# Builds vsim from source with debug mode enabled
FROM build-prep AS debug

ARG VERSION=""
RUN \
  cmake -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/work/vsim \
  -DVSIM_LINK_STATIC=ON \
  -DVSIM_DEBUG=ON \
  -DVSIM_VERSION_OVERRIDE=${VERSION} && \
  cmake --build build --target all && \
  cmake --install build


# Customer development environment, reveal platform source code but not RTL
FROM env AS dev

WORKDIR /work

COPY --from=build /work/src/ /work/src/
COPY --from=build /work/tools/ /work/tools/
# readonly config
COPY --from=build --chmod=444 /work/data/ /work/data/
COPY --from=build /work/build/ /work/build/
COPY --from=build /work/vsim/ /work/vsim/
# cmake build infrastructure (for rebuilding in dev)
COPY --from=build /work/CMakeLists.txt /work/config.yaml /work/
COPY --from=build /work/cmake/ /work/cmake/

CMD ["/bin/bash"]


# Binary only
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /work/vsim /vsim

=== build_vsim.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.
#
# What it does (README Option 3):
#   1. Build the `env` target image (verilator + toolchain) from ./Dockerfile.
#   2. Run ./build.sh inside that container with the repo bind-mounted at /work,
#      so build artifacts land in ./build/ on the host.
#
# Trim config.yaml to the CPU(s) you need first to cut build time.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# build.sh / cmake pull in external/ submodules; bail early if they are empty.
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

=== build-docker.sh ===
#!/bin/bash

# VSim Workspace Build Script
# This script builds released vsim image tar file

set -e

# arguments to docker targets
DOCKER_TARGET="$1"
if [[ ! "$DOCKER_TARGET" =~ ^(dev|runtime|bin|debug)$ ]]; then
    echo "Error: Invalid argument '$1'"
    echo "Usage: $0 {dev|runtime|bin|debug}"
    echo "  dev     - Development environment"
    echo "  runtime - Runtime environment"
    echo "  bin     - Binary only"
    echo "  debug   - debug version"
    exit 1
fi

# Generate a version file
tag=$(git describe --tags --always)
echo "vsim version : " "$tag"

if [[ "$DOCKER_TARGET" == "bin" ]]; then
    podman build --build-arg VERSION="$tag" --output=type=local,dest=andescycle-bin-"$tag" .
else
    # build image using docker or podman, archive build results
    podman build --target "$DOCKER_TARGET" --build-arg VERSION="$tag" -t andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET":"$tag" .
    podman save localhost/andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET":"$tag" | gzip > andescycle-"$DOCKER_TARGET"-"$tag".tar.gz
fi


echo "✅ Build complete"

=== config.yaml ===
# AndeSim v0.1.0 ships exactly two cycle-accurate engines. Every other CPU
# config (premium_full/max, ax46mpv_advanced, fpga_l3_bigcache_aw, d23,
# ax66_makatau) is deferred to a later release; S/U-privilege handoff went with
# ax66_makatau and is unsupported in v0.1.0 -- the hybrid leg is M-mode-only on
# both shipped engines.
cpus:
  # binary_name:
  #  rtl_package: name of external/[rtl_package]
  #  cpp_wrapper: name of the C++ wrapper class in src/cpu_wrappers/[wrapper].hpp
  #  config: path to the CPU configuration file
  #  config_dir: directory containing config.inc
  #  libaceasim_path: optional, /path/to/your/libaceasim.a , support asim if given
  ax45mpv_premium:
    cpu_series: 45
    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
  # VLEN/DLEN 1024, ELEN 64, 2 MB L3 -- the engine the Linux/ggml work is
  # validated on.
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3:
    cpu_series: 46
    rtl_package: ax46mpv_advanced
    cpp_wrapper: ax46mpv_cpu_cluster_subsystem
    config: data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg
    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run andesim inside the prebuilt Linux runtime image -- the macOS path
# (see Dockerfile.runtime; macOS is run-only, builds happen on Linux CI).
#
# Two rules make the hybrid handoff correct across the podman-machine VM:
#   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
#      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
#      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
set -euo pipefail

ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  else
    echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
    echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim-runtime:latest}"
SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim}"

TTY_ARGS=()
if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi

exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  -w "$PWD" \
  "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: on macOS the wrapper re-execs `andesim` inside the prebuilt
# Linux runtime image (both legs must share one Linux kernel). Verified on
# Linux with a stub container engine (ANDESIM_OS=Darwin forces the branch):
#
#   - the container gets --shm-size (the mmap's tier 1 lives in the VM)
#   - the caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the same path (ELF inputs/outputs)
#   - HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded (a host path would cross the VM
#     boundary, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent)
#   - the image's own baked driver is the entry; user args forward verbatim
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t andes-macos.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Stub engine: records its argv and env, runs nothing.
cat > "$TMP/stub-engine" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_OUT"
env > "$STUB_ENV"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/stub-engine"

run_wrapped() {
  (cd "$TMP" && \
   STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv" STUB_ENV="$TMP/env" \
   ANDESIM_OS=Darwin \
   ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
   HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/Users/u/scratch \
   "$ROOT/andesim" "$@" </dev/null)
}

run_wrapped run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf \
  || fail "Darwin wrapper exited non-zero"
[ -f "$TMP/argv" ] || fail "stub engine was never invoked"
ARGV=$(cat "$TMP/argv")

has() { printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx -- "$1"; }

has "run"                 || fail "engine argv missing 'run':"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--shm-size"          || fail "missing --shm-size (VM-local mmap tier 1):"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "$TMP:$TMP"           || fail "cwd not bind-mounted at the same path:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "-w"                  || fail "missing workdir:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "my.elf"              || fail "user args not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--mem-size"          || fail "user flags not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -q "andesim-runtime" \
  || fail "default runtime image name absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -q "HSIM_MMAP_DIR" \
  && fail "HSIM_MMAP_DIR must not cross into the VM:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx -- "-it" \
  && fail "no TTY here, so -it must be absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"

# ANDESIM_IMAGE overrides the image.
(cd "$TMP" && \
 STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv2" STUB_ENV="$TMP/env2" \
 ANDESIM_OS=Darwin \
 ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
 ANDESIM_IMAGE=registry.example/andes:v2 \
 "$ROOT/andesim" run --mode fast my.elf </dev/null) \
  || fail "wrapper with ANDESIM_IMAGE exited non-zero"
grep -qx "registry.example/andes:v2" "$TMP/argv2" \
  || fail "ANDESIM_IMAGE not honored:"$'\n'"$(cat "$TMP/argv2")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
#             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
#             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
#             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_lint() {
  step "[lint] harness self-checks"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/test_*.sh (each; kernel_cycles excluded)" \
      "tests/lib/roi.test.sh" "tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    # Heavy manual smoke test (real QEMU+vsim runs); e2e covers the surface.
    [ "$(basename "$s")" = "test_kernel_cycles.sh" ] && continue

# Shared status printers + config/path resolution for test scripts.
# Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#   cfg_val KEY            -> KEY's value from the repo-root config.env
#   vsim_bin_dir           -> external vsim build dir (env, then config.env)
#   qemu_bin               -> path to qemu-system-riscv64, same
#                             env-then-config.env resolution
#   shipped_cycle_engines  -> cycle-accurate engine names v0.1.0 ships
#   deferred_cycle_engines -> the ones it does not (later releases)
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# ENGINE RELEASE SURFACE -- one source of truth for the whole harness.
# v0.1.0 ships exactly two cycle-accurate engines, and the vsim side builds
# only these two (its config.yaml). Every other CPU config is deferred to a
# later release; with ax66_makatau went S/U-privilege handoff support --
# ax45mpv_premium is M-mode-only (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1) while
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 carries all three levels, so re-enabling S/U there is future
# work, not a v0.1.0 promise. test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh enforces that no
# test in the harness pins a deferred engine.
shipped_cycle_engines() { echo "ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_fpga_l3"; }
deferred_cycle_engines() {
  echo "ax45mpv_premium_full ax45mpv_premium_max ax46mpv_advanced" \
       "ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw ax66_makatau d23"
}

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

# The external QEMU build dir, resolved the same way: QEMU_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env ("" when neither is set).
qemu_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$QEMU_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR
}

# qemu_bin -> full path of qemu-system-riscv64 in that dir (AndeSim supports
# 64-bit RISC-V only).
qemu_bin() { printf '%s/qemu-system-riscv64\n' "$(qemu_bin_dir)"; }

# Quiet driver self-build (the byte-identical preamble line of every driver
# contract test). Fatal on build failure.
build_driver() {
  bash "$_LIB_ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
}

# build_driver + point BIN at the driver binary. The caller keeps its own
# [ -x "$BIN" ] assertion (the failure messages vary per script).
require_driver() {
  BIN="$_LIB_ROOT/build/andesim"
  build_driver
}

=== build_all.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#             then vlinux
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/: libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld,
#             andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
#             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
#             lib, built automatically)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
esac

=== build_driver.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andesim driver: driver/ -> build/andesim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. Consumers:
# the ./andesim wrapper (self-bootstrap on first use), scripts/test_all.sh,
# Dockerfile.runtime, and the manual tests under tests/andes_sim/,
# tests/vlinux/, and tests/plugin/. Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the
# binary is redirected to build/andesim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andesim"

=== build_runtime.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/). AndeSim supports 64-bit
# RISC-V only, so there is one output:
#   build/runtime/   libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
#                    include/andesim/ROI.h
# Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`.
#
# Self-contained: fills HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN from config.env (exported env wins),
# like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }

# Capture the exported value (it wins), then source config.env to fill the gap.
ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi
[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"

if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$SRC" TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the out-of-tree QEMU TCG plugins under qemu_plugin/:
#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)
#
# Thin wrapper over qemu_plugin/Makefile. The plugins build against the vendored
# qemu-plugin.h under qemu_plugin/include/, so NO QEMU source tree is needed --
# only the externally-built qemu-system-* binary is integrated at run time.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh [make-target...]   # e.g. clean, libhotIterationLoop.so
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

exec make -C "$ROOT/qemu_plugin" "$@"
