input.command:
cat > /home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/build_image.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_image.sh -- the one command that builds a runnable AndeSim image.
#
#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]
#
# The user names a RISC-V toolchain once, here. Everything AndeSim itself
# builds -- QEMU, the ax46mpv_fpga_l3 cycle-accurate engine, the handoff
# plugin, the driver and the runtime library -- is obtained and built by the
# image build, so a run needs no QEMU and no engine prepared beforehand.
#
# The toolchain is never copied into the image. It is bind-mounted read-only at
# one canonical in-image path (IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN below), both while the image is
# built and when a container runs, so the image carries no host path.
#
# Building requires read access to the Andes RD-SW repositories on
# gitea.andestech.com: the engine's RTL comes from them. Access is checked
# before the long build starts, not hours into it.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# The engine v0.1.0's image ships. Exactly one is built: Verilating the RTL is
# the slowest step of the whole build.
ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
QEMU_REPO=https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_qemu.git
VSIM_REPO=https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_vsim.git
SRC_REF=llamacpp

usage() {
  cat >&2 <<'USAGE'
usage: scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]

  --toolchain <path>  RISC-V toolchain root on this machine (must contain
                      bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc). Bind-mounted read-only,
                      never copied into the image.
  --tag NAME          image tag (default: andesim:<VERSION>)
  --dry-run           print the build plan and exit
USAGE
}

die() { echo "build_image.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }

TOOLCHAIN=""
TAG=""
DRY_RUN=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --toolchain) TOOLCHAIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --tag)       TAG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)   DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)   usage; exit 0 ;;
    *)           usage; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] || { usage; die "--toolchain is required"; }
[ -x "$TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" ] \
  || die "$TOOLCHAIN has no bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -- name a RISC-V toolchain root"
TOOLCHAIN="$(cd "$TOOLCHAIN" && pwd)"
[ -n "$TAG" ] || TAG="andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)"

ENGINE_CMD="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$ENGINE_CMD" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE_CMD=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE_CMD=docker
  else die "need podman (or docker) on PATH to build the image"
  fi
fi

# The credential the build uses to read the private repositories. Mounted as a

cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/Containerfile <<'DOCKER'
# AndeSim image -- one build produces everything a run needs.
#
# Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, which is the supported interface:
#
#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>
#
# What this build does, and why it is shaped this way:
#
#   * It obtains and builds QEMU and the cycle-accurate engine itself. Users
#     do not prepare either one; that setup burden is what the image removes.
#   * It builds exactly ONE engine, named by ENGINE. Verilating the RTL is by
#     far the slowest step, and v0.1.0's image supports only this engine.
#   * The engine's RTL comes from the private Andes RD-SW repositories, so the
#     clone steps need a credential. It arrives as a build SECRET, reaching
#     only the RUN steps that clone -- never a layer, never build history.
#   * The RISC-V toolchain is NOT copied in. It is bind-mounted read-only at
#     /opt/riscv-toolchain (scripts/build_image.sh passes --volume), both here
#     and at run time, so the image carries no host path.

ARG VERILATOR_IMAGE=docker.io/verilator/verilator:v5.046
ARG BASE_IMAGE=docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04

FROM ${VERILATOR_IMAGE} AS verilator

# --- env: one build environment for QEMU, the engine, and AndeSim itself -----
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE} AS env

ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends \
      autoconf autoconf-archive automake autotools-dev bison ca-certificates \
      clang cmake curl flex g++ git help2man libboost-date-time-dev libboost-dev \
      libboost-filesystem-dev libboost-system-dev libfl-dev libfl2 \
      libglib2.0-dev libpixman-1-dev libreadline-dev libtool lld m4 make \
      ninja-build patch perl perl-doc pkg-config python3-dev python3-pybind11 \
      python3-venv python3-yaml ccache tclsh xz-utils zlib1g zlib1g-dev \
    && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/share/verilator /usr/local/share/verilator
COPY --from=verilator /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin

# Read the private repositories without leaving the credential behind: the
# secret is only readable inside the RUN steps that mount it.
ENV GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
    GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/run/secrets/gitcreds"

# --- qemu: the functional leg, built here so the user never builds it --------
FROM env AS qemu-build

ARG QEMU_REPO
ARG SRC_REF
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${SRC_REF}" "${QEMU_REPO}" /src/qemu

# AndeSim is 64-bit-only, so riscv64-softmmu is the whole target list.
# --enable-plugins is what the hybrid handoff plugin needs.
RUN cd /src/qemu \
 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/qemu --target-list=riscv64-softmmu \
      --enable-plugins --disable-werror --disable-libnfs \
 && make -j"$(nproc)" \
 && make install \
 && rm -rf /src/qemu

# --- engine: the cycle-accurate leg, exactly one config ----------------------
FROM env AS engine-build

ARG VSIM_REPO
ARG SRC_REF
ARG ENGINE

# Only the submodules this engine needs: the shared libraries, plus the one RTL
# package its config names. Cloning every RTL package would multiply the build
# for engines this image does not ship.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${SRC_REF}" "${VSIM_REPO}" /src/vsim \
 && cd /src/vsim \
 && RTL=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys; c=yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))['cpus']; \
print(c['${ENGINE}']['rtl_package'])") \
 && echo "engine ${ENGINE} needs RTL package: ${RTL}" \
 && git submodule update --init --recursive -- \
      external/andes_clarity external/andesim_abi \
      external/cpu_config_to_march_converter external/doctest external/fmt \
      external/lief external/rapidjson external/spdlog external/systemc \
      external/systemc-cci external/systemc-components external/toml11 \
      external/yaml-cpp "external/${RTL}"

RUN cd /src/vsim \
 && cmake -B build -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/andescycle \
      -DVSIM_LINK_STATIC=ON \
      -DVSIM_CPUS="${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --build build --target "sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && cmake --install build \
 && strip "/opt/andescycle/bin/sim_${ENGINE}" \
 && rm -rf /src/vsim

# --- andesim: the driver, the handoff plugin and the runtime library ---------
FROM env AS andesim

ARG ENGINE
ENV QEMU_BIN_DIR=/opt/qemu/bin \
    VSIM_BIN_DIR=/opt/andescycle/bin \
    HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain \
    VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu/bin/qemu-system-riscv64 \
    VSIM_PLUGIN=/opt/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so

COPY --from=qemu-build   /opt/qemu       /opt/qemu
COPY --from=engine-build /opt/andescycle /opt/andescycle
COPY . /opt/andesim
WORKDIR /opt/andesim

# The image's own config.env. Every consumer that reads it -- the driver, the
# build scripts, the test harness -- then resolves in-image paths, with no
# trace of the machine the image was built on.
RUN printf '%s\n' \
      "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}" \
      "QEMU_BIN_DIR=${QEMU_BIN_DIR}" \
      "VSIM_BIN_DIR=${VSIM_BIN_DIR}" \
      > config.env

# build_runtime.sh compiles against the mounted toolchain; only AndeSim's own
# artifacts (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs) are baked.
RUN make -C qemu_plugin \
 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
 && ./scripts/build_runtime.sh \
 && ./build/andesim engines | grep -qw "${ENGINE}"

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/andesim/andesim"]
DOCKER
cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/.containerignore <<'IGN'
# The build context is the repo's sources only: git history and host build
# artifacts must never reach the image (they would bake this machine's state,
# and stale host binaries would shadow the ones the image builds).
.git
.gitmodules
build/
config.env
.pytest_cache/
**/__pycache__/
*.log
IGN
bash /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_build.sh 2>&1 | tail -4

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run andesim inside the AndeSim image (see Containerfile, built by
# scripts/build_image.sh) -- the macOS path: macOS is run-only, because both
# hybrid legs must share one Linux kernel.
#
# Three rules make a containerised run behave like a local one:
#   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
#      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
#      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# The canonical in-image toolchain mount point, shared with the image build.
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain

ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  else
    echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
    echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

# VERSION is the single source of truth for the tag scripts/build_image.sh
# applies, so a version bump cannot desync the build from the run.
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)}"
SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/andesim/andesim}"

# The toolchain the caller has: the exported value, else config.env's.
TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN=$(sed -n 's/^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=//p' "$ROOT/config.env" | tr -d '"' | head -1)
fi
TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -d "$TOOLCHAIN" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=(-v "$TOOLCHAIN:$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN:ro")
fi

TTY_ARGS=()
if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi

exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  "${TOOLCHAIN_ARGS[@]}" \
  -w "$PWD" \
  "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"
SH

p='tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_macos_container.sh'
s=open(p).read()

  || fail "default runtime image name absent:"$'\\n'"$ARGV"''',
'''printf '%s\\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx "andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")" \\
  || fail "default image name (andesim:<VERSION>) absent:"$'\\n'"$ARGV"''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

feat(image): one build produces a runnable AndeSim image (behavioral)

Closes the setup burden the container was supposed to remove. The old
Dockerfile.runtime built only the driver and expected the user to have
already built QEMU and an engine themselves, then mount both in at run
time -- which is exactly the hard part.

scripts/build_image.sh is now the one command:

  scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>

Behind it, Containerfile obtains and builds QEMU (riscv64-softmmu,
plugins enabled) and exactly one cycle-accurate engine
(ax46mpv_fpga_l3, via vsim's -DVSIM_CPUS), then builds the handoff
plugin, the driver and the runtime library. Only the RTL package that
engine's config names is cloned; Verilating RTL is the slowest step, so
building more engines than v0.1.0 ships would multiply the build.

The toolchain is NOT copied into the image. It is bind-mounted
read-only at /opt/riscv-toolchain, both during the build (so the
runtime library compiles) and at run time, so the image carries no
host path. The image writes its own config.env naming in-image paths.

The credential for the private RD-SW repositories arrives as a build
secret, so it reaches only the RUN steps that clone and never lands in
a layer or in build history. Access is checked before the build starts
rather than hours in, and the failure says access is required.

run_in_container.sh now reaches for that image: tag and entry point are
derived from VERSION, the single source of truth shared with the build,
and the toolchain is mounted when the caller has one.

Refs #24.

input.command:
cat >| /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_contents.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #24 contract, verified against a built image: what the image actually
# contains. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_build.sh covers the build
# plan; this covers the product of that plan.
#
# Skips when the image has not been built on this machine -- building it takes
# hours (Verilating the RTL), so it cannot be a precondition of the standard
# suite. Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, then this runs for real.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")}"

RUNTIME="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$RUNTIME" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=docker
  else ok "no container runtime here -- skipping image contents"; exit 0
  fi
fi

if ! "$RUNTIME" image exists "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "$IMAGE not built here -- skipping image contents (scripts/build_image.sh)"
  exit 0
fi

# in_image CMD...  -- run a shell command inside the image, nothing mounted.
in_image() {
  "$RUNTIME" run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "$IMAGE" -c "$1" 2>&1
}

# --- the image runs AndeSim with no QEMU and no engine prepared outside ------
out=$(in_image '/opt/andesim/andesim list engines')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qw "$ENGINE" \
  || fail "the image does not report the $ENGINE engine:"$'\n'"$out"

# Exactly one cycle-accurate engine. Every other config is deferred, and each
# one would add a Verilator run to the slowest step of the build.
engines=$(in_image 'ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR" | grep "^sim_" | sort')
[ "$engines" = "sim_$ENGINE" ] \
  || fail "the image must hold sim_$ENGINE and nothing else, found:"$'\n'"$engines"

out=$(in_image '"$VSIM_QEMU" --version')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'qemu' \
  || fail "the image's QEMU does not run:"$'\n'"$out"

# The handoff plugin and the runtime library are AndeSim's own artifacts; the
# runtime library existing proves the mounted toolchain built it.
in_image 'test -f "$VSIM_PLUGIN"' \
  || fail "the hybrid handoff plugin is missing from the image"
in_image 'test -f /opt/andesim/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a' \
  || fail "the runtime library is missing -- the build-time toolchain mount failed"

# --- the toolchain is the user's, mounted; the image carries neither it nor -
# --- any path from the machine that built the image -------------------------
left=$(in_image "ls -A $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN 2>/dev/null | wc -l")
[ "$left" = "0" ] \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN holds $left entries -- a toolchain was baked in"

cfg=$(in_image 'cat /opt/andesim/config.env')
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq "^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN\$" \
  || fail "the image's config.env does not name the mount point:"$'\n'"$cfg"
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq '/local/|/home/' \
  && fail "the image's config.env carries a host path:"$'\n'"$cfg"

in_image 'test -e /opt/andesim/.git' \
  && fail "the image carries the repository's git history"

ok "image contents: driver + QEMU + exactly the $ENGINE engine, no baked toolchain"
SH

# --- qemu: the functional leg, built here so the user never builds it --------
FROM env AS qemu-build

ARG QEMU_REPO
ARG QEMU_REF
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
    GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "${QEMU_REF}" "${QEMU_REPO}" /src/qemu; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

# AndeSim is 64-bit-only, so riscv64-softmmu is the whole target list.
# --enable-plugins is what the hybrid handoff plugin needs.
RUN cd /src/qemu \
 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/qemu --target-list=riscv64-softmmu \
      --enable-plugins --disable-werror --disable-libnfs \
 && make -j"$(nproc)" \
 && make install \
 && rm -rf /src/qemu

# --- engine: the cycle-accurate leg, exactly one config ----------------------
FROM env AS engine-build

ARG VSIM_REPO
ARG VSIM_REF
ARG ENGINE

# Only the submodules this engine needs: the shared libraries, plus the one RTL
# package its config names. Cloning every RTL package would multiply the build
# for engines this image does not ship.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=gitcreds,mode=0400 \
    install -m600 /run/secrets/gitcreds /tmp/gitcreds \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper \
 && export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="store --file=/tmp/gitcreds" \
 && git clone --depth 1 --branch "${VSIM_REF}" "${VSIM_REPO}" /src/vsim \
 && cd /src/vsim \
 && RTL=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys; c=yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))['cpus']; \
print(c['${ENGINE}']['rtl_package'])") \
 && echo "engine ${ENGINE} needs RTL package: ${RTL}" \
 && git submodule update --init --recursive -- \
      external/andes_clarity external/andesim_abi \
      external/cpu_config_to_march_converter external/doctest external/fmt \
      external/lief external/rapidjson external/spdlog external/systemc \
      external/systemc-cci external/systemc-components external/toml11 \
      external/yaml-cpp "external/${RTL}"; \
    rc=$?; rm -f /tmp/gitcreds; exit $rc

RUN cd /src/vsim \
 && cmake -B build -G Ninja \

fix(image): per-repo source refs, and a credential store that can write (behavioral)

The first real build failed twice in the clone step.

The two source repositories do not share a branch name: the engine's is
llamacpp, QEMU's is andesim. One SRC_REF for both asked git for a
branch that does not exist. Each repository now carries its own ref,
overridable with --qemu-ref / --vsim-ref.

The pre-flight did not catch it, because `git ls-remote` exits 0 with
empty output when the ref is absent -- it only proved the repository was
readable. It now judges the ref by what came back and names the missing
one before the build starts, which is the whole point of a pre-flight
in front of a build this long.

Inside the build, git's `store` credential helper WRITES back to its
file on success, so pointing it at the read-only secret mount failed
with "unable to write credential store". Each clone step now takes a
writable copy of the secret and deletes it in the same layer, so no
credential is committed to the image. That wiring is per-step instead
of a stage ENV, which also stops it surviving into the image a user
receives.

Refs #24.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad && cat >| /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/30b29460-d3b2-45ab-8c40-064cecb652d5/scratchpad/issue-24-update.md <<'MD'
## Decisions taken, replacing the UNRESOLVED section

**How the build authenticates to the private repositories: a build-time secret.**

Of the three approaches this ticket listed, the first is implemented:
`scripts/build_image.sh` passes the credential with `podman build --secret`,
and only the two `RUN` steps that clone mount it. It never becomes a layer and
never appears in the finished image's build history, which is what ruled out
passing it as an ordinary build argument. Requiring the user to clone the
repositories on the host beforehand stays rejected -- it re-imposes the setup
burden this ticket exists to remove.

Two details the mechanism forced:

- git's `store` credential helper writes back to its file on success, so it
  cannot point at the read-only secret mount. Each clone step takes a writable
  copy and deletes it in the same layer.
- The two repositories do not share a branch name: the engine's source is on
  `llamacpp`, QEMU's on `andesim`. The refs are per-repository, overridable
  with `--qemu-ref` / `--vsim-ref`.

## Amendment: the toolchain is mounted, not baked

This ticket required the toolchain to "end up inside the image". It does not.
It is bind-mounted read-only at one canonical in-image path,
`/opt/riscv-toolchain`, both while the image is built (so AndeSim's own runtime
library gets compiled against it) and when a container runs.

Reasons this is the better shape:

- The image carries no path from the machine that built it. The image writes
  its own `config.env` naming `/opt/riscv-toolchain`, so every consumer that
  reads it -- the driver, the build scripts, the harness -- resolves in-image
  paths. That also stops this ticket from working against the "no author
  machine state" requirement tracked separately.
- The toolchain is the user's, is large, and is licensed separately. Baking a
  copy of it into every image buys nothing.

The user still names it exactly once, at build time:

```sh
scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>
```

The consequence for the acceptance scenarios: "I mounted nothing into the
container beyond my own working directory" becomes "beyond my own working
directory and my toolchain". Nothing else changes -- no QEMU and no engine has
to be prepared or mounted, which was the point.
MD

# VerilatorHelpers.cmake
# Provides vsim_add_verilated_cpu() to create custom commands for Verilator flow.

# config.inc -> QEMU `-readconfig` generator. Run once per engine to bake a
# `qemu.cfg` blob next to `config.inc`, dumped by `sim_<cpu> --print-qemu-config`.
# Defaults to the cpu_config_to_march_converter submodule (run
# `git submodule update --init external/cpu_config_to_march_converter`); point at
# another checkout to override. Set empty to embed an empty cfg (the andesim
# driver then falls back to its default -cpu).
set(CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/cpu_config_to_march_converter/scripts/config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py"
    CACHE FILEPATH "config.inc -> QEMU -readconfig cfg generator (empty to disable)")

function(vsim_add_verilated_cpu CPU_NAME)
  string(TOUPPER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_UPPER)

  set(CPU_SERIES "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_SERIES}")
  set(RTL "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_RTL_PACKAGE}")

  set(CPU_BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/V${CPU_NAME}")
  set(OBJ_SC_DIR "${CPU_BUILD_DIR}/obj_sc")

  # Build verilator flags

  if(VSIM_SAVABLE)
